questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and make the given equation correct.

88 * 120 * 42 * 240 * 48 * 2
questions.solution:
According to BODMAS rule

Given equation 88 * 120 * 42 * 240 * 48 * 2

Option 1 : Using the combination =, ×, +, ÷, –

88 = 120 × 42 + 240 ÷ 48 – 2

By BODMAS rule

88 = 120 × 42 + 5 – 2

88 = 5040 + 5 – 2

88 = 5045 - 2

88 ≠ 5043 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2 : Using combination ×, ÷, =, –, +

88 × 120 ÷ 42 = 240 - 48 + 2

88 × 2.85 = 240 - 48 + 2

251.42 = 240 – 48 + 2

251.42 = 242 – 48

251.42 ≠ 194 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3 : Using the combination +, ÷, –, =, ×

88 + 120 ÷ 42 - 240 = 48 × 2

88 + 2.85 - 240 = 48 × 2

88 + 2.85 - 240 = 96

90.85 – 240 = 96

- 149.15 ≠ 96 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4 : Using the combination =, –, +, ÷, ×

88 = 120 - 42 + 240 ÷ 48 × 2

88 = 120 - 42 + 5 × 2

88 = 120 - 42 + 10

88 = 130 - 42

88 = 88 (LHS = RHS)

Hence, the answer is Option 4: “=, –, +, ÷, ×”.

questions.question: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 23 + 84 ÷ 14 × 8 − 3 = 5
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

23 + 84 ÷ 14 × 8 − 3 = 5
questions.solution:
According to the BODMAS rule:

Option 1 : ÷ and −

Given:

23 + 84 ÷ 14 × 8 − 3 = 5

After interchange the signs;

23 + 84 - 14 × 8 ÷ 3 = 5

By BODMAS rule

23 + 84 - 14 × 2.67 = 5

23 + 84 – 37.34 = 5

107 – 37.34 = 5

69.66 ≠ 5 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 2 : + and ×

Given: 

23 + 84 ÷ 14 × 8 − 3 = 5

After interchange the signs;

23 × 84 ÷ 14 + 8 − 3 = 5

By BODMAS rule

23 × 6 + 8 − 3 = 5

138 + 8 – 3 = 5

146 – 3 = 5

143 ≠ 5 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 3: − and ×

Given:

23 + 84 ÷ 14 × 8 − 3 = 5

After interchange the signs;

23 + 84 ÷ 14 - 8 × 3 = 5

By BODMAS rule

23 + 6 - 8 × 3 = 5

23 + 6 - 24 = 5

29 – 24 = 5

5 = 5 (LHS = RHS)

Option 4: − and +

Given:

23 + 84 ÷ 14 × 8 − 3 = 5

After interchange the signs;

23 - 84 ÷ 14 × 8 + 3 = 5

By BODMAS rule

23 - 6 × 8 + 3 = 5

23 – 48 + 3 = 5

26 – 48 = 5

- 22 ≠ 5 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Hence, the answer is Option 3: “− and ×”.

questions.question: What is the emigration of a significant proportion of a country’s highly-skilled, highly educated professional population to other countries offering better economic and social opportunities called?
questions.questionHtml: What is the emigration of a significant proportion of a country’s highly-skilled, highly educated professional population to other countries offering better economic and social opportunities called?
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is Brain drain.

Key Points

  • Brain drain is the emigration of a significant proportion of a country’s highly-skilled, highly educated professional population to other countries offering better economic and social opportunities.
  • It is defined as the migration of health personnel in search of a better standard of living and quality of life, higher salaries, access to advanced technology and more stable political conditions in different places worldwide.

Additional Information

  • The demographic transition theory is a generalized description of the changing pattern of mortality, fertility, and growth rates as societies move from one demographic regime to another. 
    • The demographic transition shows shifts in the demographics of a population during economic and social development. 
  • The term closed population refers to a population with no migratory flow in or out so that changes in the population occur through births and deaths only.

questions.question: Which of the following laws deduces the expression for the force between two stationary point charges in vacuum or free space?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following laws deduces the expression for the force between two stationary point charges in vacuum or free space?
questions.solution:
• Coulomb’s Law talks about the magnitude of the attraction between the two charges.

 

  • It says that the force is directly proportional to the product of the quantity of the two charges.
  • F ∝ q1q2, where (F is Force, q1 and q2 are charges).
  • It is also inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
  • i.e., F ∝ 1/r2 where (F is Force, r is the distance between the charges).
  • Thus, the equation is
  • \(F\; = \;k\frac{{{q_1}{q_2}}}{{{r_2}}}\;\)where k is the proportionality constant and is equal to 9 × 109 Nm2/C2.
  • The Law was given by Charles-Augustin de Coulomb in the year 1784.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of permanent tissue?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a characteristic of permanent tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Intercellular spaces are present.

Key Points

  • The characteristic features of permanent tissue are:
    • Cells have intercellular spaces to keep them separated.
    • The cells may be living or dead, i.e.the protoplasm is either present or absent.
    • Tissue may have only one type of cell or may have different kinds of cells.
    • The cell wall is either cellulosic or along with cellulose other complex carbohydrates may be present.
    • Cells may vary in shape, i.e., either round or oval or polygonal, etc.
    • In the living cells, the cytoplasm is present surrounding a large central vacuole.
    • Cells do not divide at all.

Additional Information

  • Types of permanent tissue: 
  • Permanent tissues are of three types, namely –
    • (a) Simple tissue, (b) Complex tissue and (c) Secretory tissue.
  • ​Simple permanent tissue
    • Simple permanent tissue is composed of a single type of cells that have comparable origin, structure, and function.
  • Types of simple permanent tissue
    • Parenchyma – It  provides temporary support and maintains the shape of the plant body. They have thin-walled cells with large vacuoles.
    • Collenchyma – It provides mechanical support and elasticity and flexibility to young dicotyledonous plants. They have thickened cell walls at corners, giving mechanical strength.
    • Sclerenchyma – It provides strength and toughness to plant parts. They have dead cells with extremely thick walls (lignin deposition). Sclerenchyma may be either fibres or sclereids
  • Complex permanent tissue
    • Complex permanent tissue is composed of two or more two types of cells and contributes to a general function.
    • They organize together to carry out similar particular functions in the plant body.
    • It is also known as vascular tissue.
  • Types of complex tissue:
    • Xylem – The xylem tissue is accountable for the transmission of water and minerals from the roots to the leaves and stems.
    • Phloem – This complex permanent tissue helps in the translocation of food that is prepared by photosynthesis in the leaves to diverse parts of the plant.

questions.question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, the bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at point E. If ∠CED = 57° and ∠A = 47°, then the measure of ∠B is:
questions.questionHtml: In a quadrilateral ABCD, the bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at point E. If ∠CED = 57° and ∠A = 47°, then the measure of ∠B is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In any quadrilateral ABCD, the angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles is equal to half the sum of the other two angles:

∠CED = (∠A + ∠B) ÷ 2

Substitute the given values ∠CED = 57° and ∠A = 47°:

57° = (47° + ∠B) ÷ 2

⇒ 114° = 47° + ∠B

⇒ ∠B = 114° − 47° = 67°

∴ The correct answer is 67°.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Quadrilateral ABCD where bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at E.

⇒ ∠CED = 57°

⇒ ∠A = 47°

Formula Used:

⇒ Angle sum property of a triangle: Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

⇒ Angle sum property of a quadrilateral: Sum of interior angles in a quadrilateral = 360°

Calculations:

In ▵CED:

⇒ ∠CED + ∠ECD + ∠EDC = 180°

⇒ 57° + ∠ECD + ∠EDC = 180°

⇒ ∠ECD + ∠EDC = 180° − 57° = 123°

Since CE and DE are the angle bisectors of ∠C and ∠D respectively:

⇒ ∠ECD = ∠C ÷ 2

⇒ ∠EDC = ∠D ÷ 2

Substituting these into the equation:

⇒ (∠C ÷ 2) + (∠D ÷ 2) = 123°

⇒ (∠C + ∠D) ÷ 2 = 123°

⇒ ∠C + ∠D = 246°

Now, using the angle sum property of quadrilateral ABCD:

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 47° + ∠B + 246° = 360°

⇒ ∠B + 293° = 360°

⇒ ∠B = 360° − 293° = 67°

Evaluation of Options:

⇒ Option (1) 47°: If ∠B = 47°, then ∠CED = (47° + 47°) ÷ 2 = 47°, which contradicts the given ∠CED = 57°.

⇒ Option (3) 77°: If ∠B = 77°, then ∠CED = (47° + 77°) ÷ 2 = 62°, which contradicts the given ∠CED = 57°.

⇒ Option (4) 57°: If ∠B = 57°, then ∠CED = (47° + 57°) ÷ 2 = 52°, which contradicts the given ∠CED = 57°.

⇒ Option (2) 67°: If ∠B = 67°, then ∠CED = (47° + 67°) ÷ 2 = 57°, which perfectly matches the given value.

∴ The correct answer is 67°.

Additional Information

Angle Bisector Theorem of Quadrilateral

The angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles: ∠CED = (∠A + ∠B) ÷ 2.

Angle Sum Property of a Polygon

The sum of the interior angles of any closed polygon with n sides is (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral, this sum is always 360°.

Opposite Angle Bisectors

If the bisectors of two opposite angles of a quadrilateral intersect, the acute angle between them is equal to half the absolute difference of the other two angles: |∠B − ∠D| ÷ 2.

questions.question: If the volume of a sphere is equal to that of a cylinder having the same radius, then find the ratio of the radius to the height of the cylinder.
questions.questionHtml: If the volume of a sphere is equal to that of a cylinder having the same radius, then find the ratio of the radius to the height of the cylinder.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Equate the volumes directly: (4/3)πr3 = πr2h

Cancel π and r2 from both sides: (4/3)r = h

Rearrange for the ratio r/h: r/h = 3/4

∴ The correct answer is 3 ÷ 4.

Alternate Method

Given: Volume of sphere = Volume of cylinder and radius of sphere = radius of cylinder = r.

Formula Used: Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr3; Volume of cylinder = πr2h

⇒ Volume of sphere = Volume of cylinder

⇒ (4/3) × π × r3 = π × r2 × h

⇒ (4/3) × r = h

⇒ r / h = 3 / 4

⇒ r ÷ h = 3 ÷ 4

∴ The correct answer is 3 ÷ 4.

Additional Information

Surface Area of Sphere

Total surface area of a sphere is given by 4πr2.

Surface Area of Cylinder

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh and Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of Cone

Volume of a cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder is (1/3)πr2h.

questions.question: Sides AB and AC of ∆ ABC are produced to points D and E, respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P. If ∠A = 78°, then the measure of ∠P is:
questions.questionHtml: Sides AB and AC of ∆ ABC are produced to points D and E, respectively. The bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P. If ∠A = 78°, then the measure of ∠P is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given, ∠A = 78°

If the bisectors of ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at P

∠P = 90° - ∠A/2

⇒ ∠P = 90° - 78°/2

⇒ ∠P = 90° - 39° = 51°

∴ The measure of ∠P is 51°

Alternate Method

Given:

∠A = 78°

Concept used:

The sum of all angles on a straight line is 180°

The sum of all angles of a triangle is 180°

Calculation:

∠ABC + ∠CBD = 180°

⇒ ∠CBD = 180° - ∠ABC

⇒ ∠CBD/2 = (180° - ∠ABC)/2

⇒ ∠CBP = 90° - ∠ABC/2  [∵ BP is the bisector of ∠CBD]

Similarly, ∠BCP = 90° - ∠ACB/2

In ΔBCP, ∠CBP + ∠BCP + ∠P = 180°

⇒ (90° - ∠ABC/2) + (90° - ∠ACB/2) + ∠P = 180°

⇒ 180° - (∠ABC + ∠ACB)/2 + ∠P = 180°

⇒ 180° - (180° - ∠BAC)/2 + ∠P = 180°

⇒ ∠P = (180° - ∠BAC)/2

⇒ ∠P = (180° - 78°)/2

⇒ ∠P = (102°)/2 = 51°

∴ The measure of ∠P is 51°

questions.question: A cyclic quadrilateral ABCD is drawn in a circle with center O. A and C are joined O. If ∠ABC = 2p and ∠ADC = 3p, what is the measure (in degrees) of the ∠AOC reflex?

questions.solution:
Given:

∠ABC = 2p and ∠ADC = 3p

Concept used:

The reflex angle is more than 180° but less than 360°

The sum of the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°

The angle at the center of a circle is twice the angle at the circumference of the circle.

Calculation:

∠ABC + ∠ADC = 180°

⇒ 2p + 3p = 180°

⇒ 5p = 180°

⇒ p = 180°/5 = 36°

So, ∠ABC = 2 × 36° = 72° and ∠ADC = 3 × 36° = 108°

Then ∠AOC = 2 × 72° = 144°  [∵ ∠ABC = 72°] (Concept used)

Another side of ∠AOC =360° - 144° = 216°

∴ The measure (in degrees) of the ∠AOC reflex is 216°

questions.question: If 8A5146B is divisible by 88, then what is the value of B - A?
questions.questionHtml: If 8A5146B is divisible by 88, then what is the value of B - A?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Number 8A5146B is divisible by 88, so it must be divisible by 8 and 11.

For divisibility by 8: Last three digits 46B must be divisible by 8 → 464 is divisible by 8, so B = 4.

For divisibility by 11: (Sum of odd places) − (Sum of even places) → (B+4+5+8) − (6+1+A) = (4+4+5+8) − (7+A) = 21 − 7 − A = 14 − A.

For 14 − A to be divisible by 11, A must be 3.

Value of B − A = 4 − 3 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given: Number = 8A5146B, Divisor = 88.

Formula Used: Divisibility rules for 8 and 11.

⇒ Divisibility by 8: 46B ÷ 8 → 8 × 5 = 40, Remainder 6. Next multiple is 64. ∴ B = 4.

⇒ Divisibility by 11: (8 + 5 + 4 + B) − (A + 1 + 6) = 0 or multiple of 11.

⇒ (17 + B) − (A + 7) = (17 + 4) − (A + 7) = 21 − 7 − A = 14 − A.

⇒ 14 − A = 11 ⇒ A = 3.

⇒ Value of B − A = 4 − 3 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Divisibility by 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the last three digits of the number are divisible by 8.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Co-prime Factors

If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers a and b, then it is also divisible by their product (a × b). Here, 8 and 11 are co-prime.
